tasks.prompt: Order a routine daily operations round at a small duplex lift station in a prairie town.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: daily attended round, no alarms active, operator records the visit on the station log sheet.

cards.label: Observe one automatic pump cycle and note the wet well levels at pump start and pump stop
Record levels, run hours, starts, and any defects in the log and raise work orders for items needing repair
Check the station exterior, access road, fencing, and any signs of vandalism, overflow, or odour on arrival
Check ventilation, heating, lighting, the building sump, and the standby generator status panel
Review the alarm history, run hours, and start counters since the last visit before touching any controls
Check each pump for abnormal noise, vibration, leakage, and discharge pressure where gauges are fitted

tasks.explanation: The round starts outside and with the recorded history, so the operator knows what changed before operating anything. Observing a real cycle and checking the support systems follow, and recording plus work orders close the visit.

tasks.prompt: Order a weekly operations round at a triplex lift station serving a growing subdivision.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: weekly attended round at a three pump station with a level transmitter, floats, and a standby generator.

cards.label: Check the chemical odour control system level if fitted and confirm dosing is operating
On arrival, walk the site and check the wet well surface for grease mats, ragging, and float fouling from above
Record all readings in the weekly log, compare run hours across the three pumps, and raise work orders for defects
Review the weekly trend of levels, flows, and alarms on the monitoring system before attending the station
Exercise the standby generator under load and record run time, fuel level, and any alarms
Run each pump in hand in turn and record current draw, discharge pressure, and any abnormal sound

tasks.explanation: Trends are reviewed first so the visit targets what is changing. Surface and pump checks prove each unit in turn, the generator is proven under load, and balanced run hours plus a complete log close the round.

tasks.prompt: Order the weekly standby generator check at a lift station.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: weekly no load and load check of an automatic standby generator at a duplex station, station stays in service throughout.

cards.label: Inspect fuel, coolant, engine oil, battery condition, and the block heater before starting the engine
Transfer back to utility power and confirm the generator cools down and shuts down on its own
Confirm the wet well level is normal and both pumps are in automatic before starting generator testing
Record the test, fuel use, and any deficiencies in the station log and arrange fuel top up if needed
Start the generator and run it unloaded, confirming voltage, frequency, and no active alarms
Transfer the station load to the generator and run the pumps, recording load and run time

tasks.explanation: The station is protected first by confirming normal levels and automatic control. Static checks precede running, load running proves the machine can carry the pumps, and transfer back plus records complete the check.

tasks.prompt: Order the response to a high level alarm at a duplex lift station at night.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: on call operator receives a high level alarm by the monitoring system and alarm dialer and attends the station. No overflow has occurred yet.

cards.label: When the level is normal, restore automatic control, confirm the alarm clears, and complete the alarm response record
Check pump control positions, breakers, and overloads, and identify why the duty pump did not start or did not keep up
Start a pump manually to draw the level down and place the second pump in automatic as backup
Acknowledge the alarm, note the time and level trend, and advise the supervisor while travelling to the station
If pumping cannot control the level, arrange bypass pumping and tanker support and notify the supervisor of overflow risk
On arrival check the wet well level, whether either pump is running, and whether any overflow has occurred at the station

tasks.explanation: Acknowledgement and notification start the response. On site, level and overflow status come before control checks, manual pumping restores control, escalation to bypass happens before an overflow if pumping is insufficient, and records close the event.

tasks.prompt: Order the response to a pump fail alarm where the tripped pump is found on overload.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: duplex station, one pump tripped on overload, the other pump is holding the wet well level.

cards.label: Check the pump and cable for damage and test the motor as permitted by site procedure before any reset
Confirm the standby pump is controlling the level and the station is not at risk before investigating the tripped pump
Reset the overload once only if no fault is found and run the pump briefly in hand while watching current draw
Check for the cause in order, starting with the wet well for rags or debris at the pump intake viewed from the surface
Return the pump to automatic if it runs normally, or leave it isolated and raise a repair work order, recording all findings
Isolate the tripped pump electrically and apply lockout before any hands on inspection

tasks.explanation: Station safety comes first because the other pump is carrying the load. Lockout precedes inspection, likely causes are checked from simplest to electrical, a single cautious reset follows only a no fault finding, and the outcome is recorded either way.

tasks.prompt: Order the lift station response to a utility power failure with a standby generator.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: storm related outage in a western Canadian town, the generator should start automatically, and the operator attends to confirm station operation.

cards.label: Confirm the outage and alarm times from the monitoring system or dialer and advise the supervisor of the affected station
Check the wet well level trend and confirm no high level or overflow condition is developing
When utility power returns, confirm transfer back, generator cooldown and shutdown, and record the event times and readings
On arrival confirm the generator is running, the transfer switch is in the emergency position, and the pumps are cycling normally
Arrange refuelling or a portable generator if the outage is expected to exceed the fuel run time
Check generator fuel, oil, coolant, and battery charger status and estimate the run time available on the fuel on hand

tasks.explanation: Remote confirmation and notification come first. On site the generator and transfer are verified before auxiliaries and levels, fuel run time drives escalation, and restoration is confirmed and logged when power returns.

tasks.prompt: Order the response to a seal fail or high temperature alarm on a submersible pump.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: duplex station, the panel shows a seal moisture and winding temperature alarm on one pump, and the pump has been stopped by its protection.

cards.label: Decide repair or replacement with the supervisor based on the inspection and keep the pump out of service until cleared
Isolate and lock out the pump if any lifting or electrical work will be done
Record the alarm type, time, run hours, and recent current readings for the alarmed pump
Record the alarm, inspection results, and the out of service status in the log and asset record
Confirm the other pump is controlling the level and place the alarmed pump control in off so it cannot restart
Arrange lifting of the pump by the approved method and inspect the seal chamber as directed by the manufacturer procedure

tasks.explanation: The healthy pump carries the station while the alarmed pump is positively prevented from restarting. Protection alarms on seals and windings mean the pump stays out until inspected, because running it risks motor failure and oil release to the flow.

tasks.prompt: Order the troubleshooting sequence when a pump runs but the wet well level does not fall.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: duplex station, the duty pump motor runs with a normal sound but the wet well level keeps rising slowly.

cards.label: Stop the pump and check the wet well intake from the surface for rags or a grease mat blocking the volute
Confirm the pump discharge valve is fully open and the correct valve lineup is in place
Leave the faulty pump isolated, record the test results, and raise a work order describing which checks were done
Check for a failed check valve or a broken discharge by watching for flow returning to the well when the pump stops
Check the discharge pressure gauge or force main pressure for a reading that suggests pumping against a closed or blocked line
Switch duty to the other pump and confirm it draws the level down, isolating the fault to the first pump or its branch

tasks.explanation: Valve lineup is the fastest external check, then pressure, then intake blockage, then return flow. Proving the twin pump narrows the fault to one branch, and the documented checks save the repair crew repeating them.

tasks.prompt: Order the investigation of repeated low level cut out and pump cavitation noise at a lift station.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the operator reports the duty pump runs past its normal stop point, is noisy, and the wet well is drawn very low each cycle.

cards.label: Clean or free the float as needed and confirm it moves freely through its full travel
Record the cause, the cleaning done, and the verified stop levels in the station log
Record the observed stop level and compare it with the design stop level and the float positions
Check the second pump stop control the same way and confirm both pumps stop correctly
Inspect the stop float from the surface for grease fouling, a tangled cable, or a float hanging up on the wall or ladder
Run a controlled cycle and confirm the pump now stops at the correct level without cavitation noise

tasks.explanation: The stop level evidence points first to the stop float, the most common cause. Cleaning and freeing it precedes a controlled proving cycle, the twin pump is checked for the same fault, and verified levels are logged.

tasks.prompt: Order the end of shift handover for a collection operator covering several lift stations.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: day operator hands over to the on call operator for the night, and two stations have open items.

cards.label: Confirm the incoming operator has read and understood the open items and note the handover in the log
Summarize active alarms, bypasses, and any station running on a single pump or on manual control
Sign off the shift record with times, names, and the items transferred
Complete all station logs and work orders for the shift before the handover discussion
Brief the incoming operator on planned night work, expected high flows, and any customer or spill follow ups pending
Pass on keys, the on call phone, radio, and the current confined space and lockout status for any open permits

tasks.explanation: Records are completed first so the handover is based on written facts. Risks and open items are briefed before equipment and permits change hands, and a signed record proves the transfer.

tasks.prompt: Order the fall winterization of a lift station before freeze up.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: October winterization visit at a duplex station with a standby generator, outdoor piping, and a long access road in a mountain valley town.

cards.label: Record the winterization checklist in the station file and list any unfinished items with dates
Check generator coolant strength, block heater, battery, and winter fuel readiness for cold starts
Inspect roof, vents, and doors for snow load damage risk and cold air leaks
Service the building heater and confirm the thermostat, fuel or power supply, and low temperature alarm all work
Confirm the access road grading, snow clearing arrangements, and the emergency fuel supply for the winter
Drain or protect outdoor water lines, sample taps, and washdown hoses that can freeze

tasks.explanation: Winterization is a system check, not a single task: heat, water lines, generator cold starting, the building shell, and road access each get verified. Unfinished items are listed with dates because freeze up does not wait for a convenient week.

tasks.prompt: Order a manhole inspection from the surface, starting before the cover is removed.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: routine condition inspection of a sanitary manhole on a residential street, surface inspection only, no entry planned.

cards.label: Set up traffic control and barriers suited to the street before opening the cover
Observe flow depth and condition and note any surcharge, grease, roots, or infiltration seen
Review the asset record and previous inspection notes for the manhole before leaving the yard
Close and seat the cover fully, remove traffic control, and complete the inspection record the same day
Ventilate at the opening and test the atmosphere at the opening before leaning over the manhole
Inspect the cover, frame, walls, joints, benching, and channel from the surface and note defects in standard terms

tasks.explanation: History and safe setup come before the cover is opened. Atmosphere testing precedes any work at the opening, observations follow a fixed order so nothing is missed, and the record is completed while the findings are fresh.

tasks.prompt: Order the safe opening of a manhole cover in a travelled lane for a short inspection.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: brief surface inspection of a manhole located in one lane of a two lane road, two person crew.

cards.label: Reseat the cover flush, confirm it does not rock, remove traffic control in reverse order, and record the visit
Lift the cover with the correct hook tool using leg power and slide it clear without dragging it across the opening
Test the atmosphere at the opening and ventilate before the inspection begins
Place advance warning signs, cones, and barriers to close the lane before any worker steps into the travelled way
Complete the inspection promptly from the surface with the opening guarded at all times
Position a spotter facing traffic and confirm radio or hand signal communication with the worker at the cover

tasks.explanation: Traffic is controlled before anyone enters the lane, and the opening is never left unguarded. Correct lifting protects the worker, testing precedes inspection, and a flush, quiet cover plus orderly teardown close the job.

tasks.prompt: Order the measurement of flow depth and estimation of surcharge condition in a manhole.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: operator measures depth of flow in a trunk manhole during dry weather to check for downstream restriction.

cards.label: Compare the measured depth with the expected dry weather depth for that time of day
Set up traffic control, open the cover safely, and test the atmosphere at the opening
Look upstream and downstream for signs of surcharge, such as debris lines above the normal flow level
Record the pipe diameter from the asset record and calculate the depth as a proportion of diameter
Record the measurements, the comparison, and any follow up cleaning or inspection raised
Measure the depth of flow from the cover rim using a marked rod lowered to the channel invert

tasks.explanation: Safe opening comes first, then a measurement tied to a fixed reference. Expressing depth against diameter and against the expected dry weather pattern is what turns a number into a surcharge judgement, and the record supports the follow up.

tasks.prompt: Order the documentation of defects found during a manhole inspection.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: inspector has completed a surface inspection and found joint infiltration, benching damage, and a corroded step. Photos were taken during the inspection.

cards.label: Confirm each photo is labelled with the manhole asset number, date, and direction of view before leaving the site
Enter the inspection into the asset system the same day and attach the labelled photos
Flag the manhole for re-inspection after repair and note the follow up date in the record
Record each defect with its location in the structure, its extent, and a severity rating in standard terms
Raise work orders for repairs, ranked by hazard first and then by infiltration or structural impact
Note any defect that is an immediate hazard, such as a broken cover or a missing step, for urgent action

tasks.explanation: Photos are useless without asset labels, so labelling is confirmed on site. Defects are recorded in standard terms with severity, hazards are escalated ahead of routine repairs, and re-inspection closes the loop.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps after a manhole inspection finds the cover and frame broken and sitting below road grade.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: arterial road manhole, the frame is cracked, the cover rocks under traffic, and the top sits about 40 mm below the pavement.

cards.label: Complete the repair, set the new frame to grade, and confirm the cover sits flush and quiet under traffic
Inspect the frame seat and chimney from the surface to judge whether adjustment rings or a full frame replacement is needed
Notify the supervisor and the roads group of the hazard and record the report time and location
Record the repair, materials used, and final grade in the asset record and close the hazard report
Place cones and a steel plate or barrier over the damaged cover at once to protect traffic and pedestrians
Schedule the frame and cover replacement with traffic control planned for the road class and time of day

tasks.explanation: A broken cover in a travelled way is a public hazard first and a maintenance job second, so protection and notification come before assessment. Repair is planned for the road conditions, set to grade, and documented.

tasks.prompt: Order a wet weather manhole check for infiltration at the joints and connections.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: during spring rain, the crew checks manholes in an older sewershed known for high wet weather flows.

cards.label: Observe each joint and pipe connection for clear water weeping, dripping, or running into the manhole
Select manholes from the sewershed map where infiltration is suspected, starting with the oldest sections
Record all findings by asset number and rank the manholes for sealing or rehabilitation follow up
Estimate each infiltration rate in general terms and photograph active leaks with the asset number recorded
Set up traffic control, open each cover safely, and test the atmosphere at each opening
Note whether flow rises quickly with rain, which suggests inflow, or stays elevated after rain, which suggests infiltration

tasks.explanation: Wet weather is the only time joint infiltration is fully visible, so the route targets suspect structures while it rains. Each leak is located, estimated, and photographed, and the rain response pattern separates inflow from infiltration for the follow up ranking.

tasks.prompt: Order the pre-rehabilitation assessment of a manhole selected for lining or sealing.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: manhole is a candidate for a cured lining and chemical grout sealing in the annual rehabilitation program.

cards.label: Record wall material, depth, pipe sizes and inverts, and the condition of benching and channel
Complete the assessment form with photos and recommend lining, sealing, or full replacement with reasons
Review the inspection history, infiltration records, and any CCTV notes for the connecting pipes
Confirm access for rehabilitation equipment, including space for hoses and ventilation at the site
Set up traffic control, open the cover safely, test the atmosphere, and measure the structure dimensions from the surface
Identify active infiltration points and note whether flows must be plugged or bypassed during lining

tasks.explanation: The rehabilitation method depends on dimensions, materials, and active leaks, all gathered in a fixed order after the history is reviewed. Access and flow control needs are confirmed before a method is recommended, so the program is not priced on surprises.

tasks.prompt: Order manhole checks in a low lying area during spring melt ponding.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: meltwater is ponding over several manholes in a low area of a prairie town, and inflow through covers is suspected.

cards.label: Install raised or sealed covers or sandbagging at the worst inflow points as directed by the supervisor
Check each ponded manhole from the edge of the ponded area without wading into deep water over an open structure
Record each location, the action taken, and the station flow response for the melt season file
Review the melt forecast and identify the low manholes from the sewershed map before going out
Check the downstream lift station flows to confirm whether melt inflow is reaching the station
Note covers that are displaced, vent holes taking meltwater, or flow audible through the cover

tasks.explanation: Ponded meltwater hides open structures, so locations come from the map and checks are made from safe ground. Confirming the effect at the lift station proves the inflow matters, quick sealing reduces it, and the melt file guides next year.

tasks.prompt: Order the inspection of benching and channel condition during a manhole surface inspection.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: older brick manhole on a collector sewer, inspection is from the surface with a light and mirror, no entry.

cards.label: Shine the light across the benching and note cracking, missing mortar, or sections broken away
Photograph the defects with a scale reference and record their clock positions and depths
Set up traffic control, open the cover, ventilate at the opening, and test the atmosphere
Record the findings, raise repair work orders for benching or channel defects, and close the cover securely
Check the channel for a smooth, shaped flow path and note any lip, offset, or debris catching edge
Observe a flow period and note whether solids deposit on the benching or swirl instead of passing through

tasks.explanation: Benching and channel defects cause deposits and blockages upstream of any pipe defect, so they are inspected deliberately, not in passing. Watching real flow confirms whether the defect matters, and photos with positions let the repair crew find the damage.

tasks.prompt: Order the closeout steps after a day of manhole inspections on a residential route.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: crew has inspected twelve manholes, two covers were left flagged for repair, and the records must be finished before the shift ends.

cards.label: File the completed route record and record crew time and equipment use on the work order
Enter or upload all inspections, photos, and defect ratings into the asset system
Pass the two flagged cover hazards to the supervisor with locations for urgent repair scheduling
Confirm every manhole visited has its cover fully seated and the site left clean and safe
Note any manholes that could not be opened, with the reason, for a return visit with the right equipment
Check the inspection forms against the route list so no scheduled manhole was missed

tasks.explanation: Public safety is confirmed first, because a poorly seated cover is a hazard the crew created. Completeness checks against the route list prevent silent gaps, hazards are handed over the same day, and filing closes the work.

tasks.prompt: Order a sewer flushing operation using a hydrant and flushing bag on a flat residential sewer.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: low gradient 200 mm residential sewer with grit and light debris, flushed from the upstream manhole toward the downstream manhole.

cards.label: Release water in controlled surges so the wave carries debris downstream without surcharging services
Confirm the downstream manhole is accessible and set up traffic control at both manholes
Watch the downstream manhole and stop flushing when the flow runs clear and the debris wave has passed
Connect the flushing bag and hose to the hydrant and confirm the water supply and backflow protection are in place
Remove the trap and debris for disposal, record the length flushed and debris volume, and secure both covers
Open both covers safely, test the atmosphere at each opening, and place a debris trap or screen at the downstream manhole

tasks.explanation: Both ends are prepared before water moves, because flushed debris must be caught, not pushed into the next section. Controlled surges protect services from surcharge, clear flow signals completion, and capture plus records close the job.

tasks.prompt: Order a high pressure jetting pass to clean a gravity sewer from the downstream manhole.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: combination jet vacuum truck cleaning a 300 mm collector with grit and grease, working upstream from the downstream manhole.

cards.label: Set up traffic control, open the downstream manhole safely, and confirm the section length and pipe size from the map
Retrieve the hose slowly so the jets pull debris back to the downstream manhole while the vacuum removes it
Record the section cleaned, passes made, and debris removed, and secure the manhole covers
Select the nozzle for cleaning rather than cutting and set the pump pressure for the pipe material and condition
Repeat passes until the return flow runs clear and little debris reaches the vacuum
Insert the hose and advance the nozzle upstream at a steady pace to the upstream manhole or the full hose length

tasks.explanation: The jet cleans on the retrieve, not on the advance, so nozzle choice, pressure, and a slow retrieve control the result. Working from downstream keeps debris moving toward the vacuum, and clear return flow is the completion test.

tasks.prompt: Order the jetting response when the nozzle will not advance past a point partway upstream.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: during a cleaning pass the nozzle stops advancing about halfway along the section and pressure rises.

cards.label: Choose the next method with the supervisor, such as a different nozzle, rodding, or CCTV to identify the obstruction
Check the nozzle for damage and note the distance reached from the hose counter
Reduce pressure and retrieve the hose fully to the downstream manhole
Record the location reached, the suspected cause, and the follow up method in the work order
Stop advancing and work the hose back and forth a short distance to try to free the nozzle without forcing it
Inspect from the upstream manhole if accessible to see the obstruction from the other side

tasks.explanation: Forcing a stuck nozzle risks a broken hose or a damaged pipe, so the first moves free and then retrieve it. Measuring the distance locates the problem, the far side is checked, and the next method is chosen on evidence, not guesswork.

tasks.prompt: Order the debris capture and disposal steps at the downstream manhole during a jetting operation.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: jetting is under way on a grit heavy section and debris is arriving at the downstream manhole where the vacuum truck is positioned.

cards.label: Stop jetting when the tank nears capacity and decant liquid back to the manhole as permitted before hauling solids
Position the vacuum tube at the channel outlet so debris is captured as it arrives, before it can pass downstream
Record debris volume, disposal location, and the sections completed on the cleaning work order
Haul collected grit and debris to the approved disposal site and obtain the disposal record
Keep the vacuum running during each retrieve pass and watch the debris load in the tank sight glass
Wash down the manhole channel and benching so no loosened debris is left to move downstream

tasks.explanation: Capture at the outlet is the point of downstream jetting, so vacuum position and timing come first. Tank capacity governs the work rhythm, disposal is documented, and the manhole is left clean so the cleaning does not create the next blockage.

tasks.prompt: Order the cleaning of a grease choked sewer section found during a blockage call.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: 250 mm sewer behind a row of food service businesses, flow is passing slowly past a heavy grease deposit.

cards.label: Jet from downstream with a grease cutting nozzle in short passes, vacuuming grease and debris at the downstream manhole
Record the section, the businesses upstream, and recommend a follow up inspection and a shorter cleaning interval
Set up traffic control and open the downstream and upstream manholes safely with atmosphere testing at each opening
Dispose of the grease laden debris at the approved site, since it cannot go back into the system
Confirm the extent of the grease from both ends and warn the supervisor if flow is close to surcharging services
Continue passes until the pipe wall is visible in the return flow and flow passes freely

tasks.explanation: Extent is confirmed from both ends before cutting starts, and grease is always removed at the downstream manhole, never pushed ahead. A free flowing pipe is the completion test, and the record links the hotspot to its sources for prevention.

tasks.prompt: Order a root cutting operation in a sewer using a jet driven rotary cutter.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: 200 mm clay sewer with roots confirmed at several joints by an earlier CCTV survey, flow is still passing.

cards.label: Retrieve slowly while vacuuming the cut roots at the downstream manhole so they cannot form a new blockage
Set up traffic control, open both manholes safely, and confirm downstream vacuum capture is ready
Record the joints treated and recommend a follow up CCTV check and a root control interval for the section
Review the CCTV record to mark the chainage of each root mass before setting up
Advance the rotary cutter to each marked root mass and work it through slowly until the roots are cut flush
Run a plain jetting pass first to clean the pipe so the cutter works on roots, not on debris

tasks.explanation: Cutting is targeted from the survey record, not done blind. A cleaning pass first, slow cutting at marked joints, and capture of every cut root prevent the cure from becoming the next blockage, and follow up is scheduled from the record.

tasks.prompt: Order the planning sequence for a preventive sewer cleaning program visit to a street segment.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: office planning the day before a scheduled preventive cleaning route covering six sections in an older neighbourhood.

cards.label: Check manhole access on the map and note buried, paved over, or easement manholes needing extra equipment
Load the correct nozzles, hoses, and traffic control for the pipe sizes and conditions expected
Pull the cleaning history and CCTV records for the segment and rank sections by past debris, roots, and grease
Issue the route work order with the ranked sections and record the plan for the crew briefing
Confirm water supply points, disposal site hours, and the truck route for the day
Notify affected residents or businesses where access or short traffic delays are expected

tasks.explanation: Preventive work succeeds on preparation: history sets the priorities, access and logistics are confirmed before the truck rolls, and the crew leaves with the right tools and a ranked route instead of discovering problems section by section.

tasks.prompt: Order the post cleaning flow restoration check after clearing a sewer blockage.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a mainline blockage has just been cleared by jetting and the upstream manhole was surcharged to near the rim.

cards.label: Record the cause found, the method used, and the sections cleaned, and flag the section for follow up if the cause is structural
Check the nearest upstream services or the caller property to confirm drainage is restored, where access is given
Inspect the downstream manhole to confirm no debris slug was pushed into the next section
Watch the upstream manhole level fall to normal and confirm flow passes the cleared section freely
Restore both manholes, remove traffic control, and confirm no sewage remains on the surface
Run a final jetting pass through the section and vacuum the manhole until the return flow is clear

tasks.explanation: Clearing the blockage is not the finish: levels must return to normal, the section must pass a final clean pass, and downstream must be checked for a moved blockage. Confirmation at the affected property and a cause record close the call properly.

tasks.prompt: Order a vacuum truck decant and disposal sequence at the end of a cleaning shift.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: combination truck returns to the works yard with a tank of grit, debris, and decant water from the day cleaning route.

cards.label: Wash the tank, vacuum tubes, and screens and inspect for damage or blockages
Park at the approved decant area and confirm the receiving point is the designated sewer or drying bed, not a storm drain
Complete the disposal record with volumes, source sections, and the disposal location
Open the tank and discharge the solids into the designated bin or bed using the washdown hose
Refill the water tank, refuel, and report any defects so the truck is ready for the next shift
Decant the liquid portion slowly to the approved point while keeping solids in the tank

tasks.explanation: Decanting to the wrong drain returns the load to the wrong system, so the receiving point is confirmed first. Liquids and solids are separated in order, the truck is left clean and ready, and the disposal record accounts for the material.

tasks.prompt: Order the setup for cleaning a sewer on an easement behind houses with no road access.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: 200 mm sewer on a rear lot easement, the nearest road access is 80 m from the downstream manhole, and portable equipment must be used.

cards.label: Notify the affected property owners of the work dates and confirm gate and yard access in advance
Open the downstream manhole safely, test the atmosphere, and set up debris capture before cleaning starts
Restore yards and fences, secure the covers, and record access notes for the next visit in the asset record
Walk the easement to confirm manhole locations, ground conditions, and a safe equipment path that protects fences and landscaping
Clean in short sections, hauling debris back to the road staging point for disposal
Stage portable jetting and vacuum equipment at the nearest road point and lay hoses along the agreed path

tasks.explanation: Easement work fails on access, not on cleaning, so owners, the route, and staging are settled before equipment moves. Debris capture still comes before cleaning, and access notes make the next visit faster.

tasks.prompt: Order the decision sequence for cleaning before CCTV inspection of a problem sewer.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a 300 mm collector with two blockages in a year is scheduled for CCTV, and the operator must decide how much cleaning the camera needs.

cards.label: If heavy deposits remain, repeat cleaning or record that the survey will be limited and why
Jet the section from downstream and vacuum at the downstream manhole until the return flow runs reasonably clear
Check flow depth at the downstream manhole, since a surcharged or very deep flow will hide the pipe wall from the camera
Record the cleaning done and the pipe condition handed over to the CCTV crew in the work order
Review the blockage history and any earlier CCTV to judge the likely debris, roots, and grease load
Confirm the pipe is clean enough that the camera can see the walls and joints for the full section

tasks.explanation: A camera survey of a dirty pipe records debris, not defects, so history and flow depth judge the cleaning needed. Cleaning precedes the survey, readiness is confirmed honestly, and limitations are recorded rather than hidden.

tasks.prompt: Order the setup and calibration steps before a CCTV inspection run.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: mainline CCTV crew setting up at the downstream manhole for a 90 m section survey in a residential area.

cards.label: Set the distance counter to zero at the entry point and confirm it against a measured length
Set up traffic control and open both manholes safely with atmosphere testing at each opening
Begin the run at the controlled survey speed only when header, counter, picture, and communication are all confirmed
Check camera picture, lighting, and focus in the pipe entry and confirm the recording system is capturing
Confirm the asset numbers, pipe size, material, and survey direction from the map and enter them in the survey header
Confirm communication between the camera operator and the surface crew at the far manhole

tasks.explanation: Survey data is only as good as its header and distance accuracy, so identification, counter, and picture checks all precede travel. Communication with the far crew protects the cable and the camera, and the run starts only when every check passes.

tasks.prompt: Order the camera work during a CCTV run when a defect is found partway along the pipe.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: at about 40 m the camera shows a cracked pipe section with soil visible and slight deformation.

cards.label: Record the distance from the counter and note the clock positions and length of the defect in standard coding terms
Flag the defect in the survey notes for engineering review because of the visible soil and deformation
Stop the camera travel at the defect and hold position so the defect stays in clear view
Continue the survey at normal speed once the defect is fully documented
Pan and tilt or rotate the camera head to show the full extent of the crack around the pipe wall
Zoom or adjust lighting to confirm whether soil is visible and whether infiltration is active at the defect

tasks.explanation: A defect passed at travel speed is a defect half recorded, so the camera stops and documents extent, position, and distance before moving on. Visible soil and deformation raise the urgency, so the survey flags the defect for review the same day.

tasks.prompt: Order the CCTV workflow when the camera cannot complete the run because of debris in the pipe.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the camera stops at 55 m of a 90 m section against a heavy grit and debris deposit it cannot pass.

cards.label: If the section still cannot be completed, survey from the upstream manhole in reverse to cover the missed length
Retrieve the camera carefully without forcing it through the deposit
Record both survey parts, the cleaning done, and any length still unsurveyed in the report
Record the distance reached and code the survey as incomplete with the reason at the point the camera stopped
Re-run the camera from the downstream end to complete the remaining length if the pipe is now passable
Jet the section from downstream and vacuum the debris at the downstream manhole

tasks.explanation: Forcing a camera buries it, so the incomplete point is coded and the camera is recovered first. Cleaning and a re-run, or a reverse survey, complete the coverage, and any gap is stated plainly in the report.

tasks.prompt: Order the defect coding and report completion steps after a CCTV survey shift.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: operator returns with surveys of eight sections, including two with structural defects needing review.

cards.label: Review each run and confirm every defect has a distance, clock position, and standard code
Write the shift summary noting incomplete surveys and the reasons, with follow up cleaning or re-survey raised
Check each survey video plays and matches its header asset number before leaving the site data on the truck system
Back up the survey data as required and close the work orders for completed sections
Rank the defects by severity and flag structural defects and active infiltration for engineering review
Transfer the videos and coded data to the asset system and confirm the transfer is complete

tasks.explanation: Data is verified before it leaves the truck, because a lost or mislabelled survey means a return visit. Coding is checked for completeness, serious defects are flagged the same day, and summaries state gaps honestly.

tasks.prompt: Order a lateral launch camera inspection from a mainline sewer, at an awareness level.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a service lateral is suspected of contributing infiltration, and a launch camera is used from the mainline under a trained CCTV operator.

cards.label: Record the lateral survey against both the mainline asset and the property address for follow up
Launch the lateral camera into the service slowly, watching for joints, connections, and active infiltration
Stop and document any defect with its distance from the mainline connection
Confirm the mainline survey has located the lateral connection and recorded its distance and clock position
Retrieve the lateral camera fully into the launcher before moving the mainline camera
Position the launch camera at the connection and confirm picture and distance counter for the lateral unit

tasks.explanation: The lateral survey depends on the mainline record for its starting point, so location comes first. The small camera is fully retrieved before the main unit moves, and the record links the lateral to the property so follow up reaches the right owner.

tasks.prompt: Order the quality check of CCTV data before it is accepted into the asset system.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: supervisor or senior operator reviews a contractor CCTV submission covering twenty sections before payment processing.

cards.label: Confirm distances are plausible for the section lengths and defects carry standard codes
Check the submission list against the work order so every requested section is present
List any sections that fail the checks and return them for re-survey with the reasons stated
Confirm headers show the correct asset numbers, pipe sizes, materials, and survey directions
Accept the passing surveys into the asset system and record the acceptance and the exceptions
Play samples from each survey and confirm the picture is clear enough to see joints and defects

tasks.explanation: Acceptance is a check, not a filing step: completeness, picture quality, headers, and coding are verified in order, failures go back with reasons, and only passing data enters the asset record that future decisions rely on.

tasks.prompt: Order an emergency CCTV inspection to locate a blockage in a sewer with a backup in progress.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: homes are backing up on a street, jetting has restored partial flow, and the camera is needed to find the cause before it recurs.

cards.label: Confirm flow is passing and levels are falling so the camera can travel and the crew can work safely
Run the camera upstream at survey speed, watching for roots, grease, debris, or a collapsed section
Record the emergency survey and the recommended repair or cleaning follow up in the incident file
Set up traffic control and open the downstream manhole safely with atmosphere testing
Stop at the cause, document its distance and condition, and report it to the supervisor at once
Enter the survey header quickly and confirm picture and distance counter before launching

tasks.explanation: Even in an emergency the camera needs passing flow, a correct header, and a true distance to be useful. Finding and documenting the cause during the same visit prevents a second backup, and the incident file carries the follow up.

tasks.prompt: Order the surface support duties for a CCTV crew working between two manholes.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a two person surface crew supports the camera operator, manages the cable, and guards the open manholes during a survey on a collector road.

cards.label: Keep the public away from the openings and the cable path during the run
Feed the cable smoothly without kinks or dragging over the frame edge as the camera advances
Confirm radio communication with the camera operator and agree the signals for advance, stop, and retrieve
Recover and clean the cable as it is retrieved and secure both covers when the survey is complete
Set up traffic control at both manholes and confirm barriers guard each open cover for the whole survey
Watch the far manhole for the camera arrival light and report it to the operator

tasks.explanation: Surface support protects the public, the cable, and the survey quality at the same time. Communication is agreed before movement starts, openings stay guarded throughout, and clean recovery leaves the equipment ready for the next run.
